name: TabBar
purpose: Specialized mobile bottom navigation bar. For three-end chrome use Navigation (one list, CSS morph). Do not pair this with Sidebar to fake a morph.
scenarios: Switch between the three to five top-level destinations on a phone
Keep primary navigation reachable by the thumb
Mirror navigation order in RTL locales

label.description: Accessible name of the navigation landmark.

items.description: Array of destinations with value and label.

states.name: default
states.description: One destination is active; the bar is docked to the block-end edge.

antiPatterns: Do not use for content switching inside a page; use tabs.
Do not exceed five destinations in the bar.
Do not compose TabBar with Sidebar for three-end chrome — that is two components. Use Navigation.
Do not keep the bar visible at desktop when composed in app-shell's legacy slot — that slot hides at 80rem.

keyboard: Tab moves to the active destination
Arrow keys move between destinations (roving tabindex via the tabs primitive)
a11y.focus: Roving tabindex and direction-aware arrow keys are delegated to Ark UI / Zag; visible focus ring on items.
a11y.labeling: The bar is labelled via its label prop; each destination is labelled by its visible text.

responsive.strategy: Single-form compact bar docked to the block-end edge with env(safe-area-inset-bottom) padding. Named container tab-bar shrinks labels at 20rem. Three-end morph is Navigation, not a pair with Sidebar.

breakpoints.compact: Bottom bar; every item hit area >= 44px; safe-area bottom inset applied.
breakpoints.medium: Still this bar if rendered directly; AppShell's legacy tabBar slot stays visible until 80rem.
breakpoints.large: AppShell's legacy tabBar slot is hidden; use Navigation for a persistent sidebar form.

rtl.strategy: Logical CSS only; item order follows the document direction and arrow-key roving is direction-aware via the primitive.
